The Windows .zip also holds two files that are not part of the jkit binary: vcruntime140.dll and
vcruntime140_1.dll, the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime that jkit.exe uses. They are Microsoft's
redistributable files, copied unchanged from Microsoft Visual Studio and signed by Microsoft.

  Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

They are not covered by jkit's MIT License or by any other license in this file. Microsoft allows
them to be distributed with a program that uses them, under the "Distributable Code" terms of the
Microsoft Software License Terms for Visual Studio (https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/license-terms/).
Those terms carry over to anyone who distributes them further: if you pass these two files on, you
must not

- change them, or any copyright, trademark or patent notice in them;
- use Microsoft's trademarks in your program's name, or in a way that suggests your program comes
  from or is endorsed by Microsoft;
- distribute them to run on anything other than Microsoft Windows;
- include them in a malicious, deceptive or unlawful program; or
- combine or distribute them so that any part of them becomes subject to a license that requires
  source code to be disclosed, or that they be licensed for modification or distributed free.

and you must require those you give them to to agree to terms that protect them at least as much
as these.

You don't need them if the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (2015 or later, x64) is installed:
delete both files and install it instead, with `winget install Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x64` or
from https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe. Windows Update then keeps it patched.
